Qwen/Qwen3-8B.notes:
Confidence set to 'low' per the stub rule, and the flag is about the CARD, not about the distillation claim. The card is entirely silent on training method: it says only '- Training Stage: Pretraining & Post-training' and never mentions SFT, DPO, RL, RLHF, or distillation. Everything under method/algorithm/datasets comes from the technical report, which names Qwen3-8B directly and is therefore strong evidence — I would not want the 'low' read as doubt that the 8B is a distillation.

CARD-VS-PAPER: not a contradiction, but a gap that invites one. The card's marketing bullets ('Significantly enhancement in its reasoning capabilities', 'Superior human preference alignment') read like the output of an RLHF pipeline, and the family paper prominently documents a four-stage SFT+RL process. That process is NOT this checkpoint's. PAPER: 'As illustrated in Figure 1, the flagship models in the Qwen3 series follow a sophisticated four-stage training process.' and, for the lightweight track, 'For smaller models, we use strong-to-weak distillation, leveraging both off-policy and on-policy knowledge transfer from larger models to enhance their capabilities.' The 8B is enumerated in the lightweight list.

ALGORITHM left 'unknown' deliberately. GRPO appears in the report — 'We ultimately collect a total of 3,995 query-verifier pairs, and employed GRPO (Shao et al. 2024) to update the model parameters' — but that sentence sits in the flagship Reasoning RL stage, not in the distillation section, so it cannot be attached to Qwen3-8B. The 3,995 pairs likewise belong to the flagship stage and are not this checkpoint's train_tokens. The distillation itself is described as off-policy response distillation followed by on-policy KL-minimising logit alignment; no named optimiser distinct from the operation is given.

STAGE CHECKPOINTS: none released — there is no separate Qwen3-8B-SFT or -DPO. If the roster needs a base→SFT→DPO decomposition, this lineage supports only base→aligned, and the aligned endpoint is a distillation rather than a preference-optimisation product.

License verified at file level: the repo's LICENSE is the Apache License Version 2.0.

From-scratch status is established by the paper (§6), which describes the 360M as separately trained with its own data ablations, architecture variant (GQA) and WSD scheduler; no parent checkpoint is named in card or paper, and training framework is nanotron on 128 H100. SCOPE NOTE, not a contradiction: the paper abstract says "we overtrain SmolLM2 on ~11 trillion tokens" — that figure is for the 1.7B; §6 gives 4T for the 360M, matching the card. The reasoning=no claim is absence-based: neither card nor paper describes any chain-of-thought or reasoning-targeted stage for this model; the word "reasoning" appears on the card only in a benchmark-capability sentence ("particularly in instruction following, knowledge, reasoning"), which I have deliberately not used as evidence. CARD-VS-PAPER: the card names the corpus as "FineWeb-Edu, DCLM, The Stack, along with new filtered datasets we curated and will release soon", while the paper §6 names those later-released sets explicitly (Stack-Edu, InfiMM-WebMath, FineMath, Cosmopedia) and specifies DCLM was filtered with the FineWeb-Edu classifier. These are consistent, the paper is more specific.

OpenLLM-France/Lucie-7B.notes: ROOT, AND THE INDEPENDENCE VERDICT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART OF THIS AUDIT. The card contains one sentence that could be misread as derivation: "Lucie-7B has the same neural network architecture as [Llama3.1](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B)." That is an ARCHITECTURE statement, not a weights-initialisation statement, and three facts on the same card rule out any continuation of Meta's checkpoint: (a) vocabulary size is 65 024, against Llama-3.1-8B's 128 256 — a different tokenizer means the embedding and unembedding matrices cannot be inherited; (b) parameter count is "exactly 6 706 958 336 free parameters", not 8B; (c) the hyperparameter table lists "| Initializer range         | 0.009        |", a random-initialisation parameter that is meaningless for continued pretraining, alongside 753,851 steps of main pre-training from a warmup+cosine schedule at max LR 3e-4 (a from-scratch LR, not a continuation LR). Compute is consistent with scratch training: "It was pre-trained on 512 H100 80GB GPUs for about 550\,000 GPU hours on the [Jean Zay supercomputer](http://www.idris.fr/eng/jean-zay/jean-zay-presentation-eng.html)." Own training code (OpenLLM-France/Lucie-Training, a fork of Megatron-DeepSpeed) and own released pretraining corpus. COUNTS AS AN INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION. Training is three phases (main pre-training, context extension to 32k, annealing on 5B tokens of high-quality data), so the released base is post-annealing, not a raw main-phase checkpoint — relevant if the roster treats annealed bases differently. No card-vs-paper contradiction: arXiv:2503.12294 calls it "the Lucie-7B foundation model". Intermediate/step checkpoints are available in the repo per the card's "Load a checkpoint" section.

OpenLLM-France/Lucie-7B-Instruct-v1.1.notes: SFT-ONLY, AND THE CARD SAYS SO NEGATIVELY AS WELL AS POSITIVELY. This is not an instruct_bundle: the card explicitly places preference optimisation in the FUTURE, i.e. outside this checkpoint — "Its performance and accuracy can be improved through further fine-tuning and alignment with methods such as DPO, RLHF, etc." The base card's disclaimer says the same from the other side: "To limit such behavior, it is advised to fine-tune Lucie-7B through instruction and/or preference tuning (DPO, RLHF, etc.)." So for a base->ego->superego topology this lineage supplies an EGO ONLY; there is no DPO/superego checkpoint in it. The card also downgrades the intervention's depth: "Note that this instruction training is light and is meant to allow Lucie to produce responses of a desired type (answer, summary, list, etc.)." DIRECTION IS RETURNED AS unknown, DELIBERATELY, and this is a gap rather than a judgement: the card never discusses refusal behaviour, safety data, or de-censoring in either direction. What can be said is descriptive only — the documented mixture is enumerated and exhaustive ("Lucie-7B-Instruct-v1.1 is trained on the following datasets:") and contains no toxic-DPO or uncensored component, and the single documented filter is identity-related, not safety-related: "This filter is designed to remove examples in which the assistant is presented as model other than Lucie (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemma, Llama, ...)." That is absence of a de-censoring mixture, which is not the same as a sourced "standard" alignment intent, so I did not book it as one. Note also that NO safety dataset appears in the mixture at all — if the roster codes an explicit safety component, this checkpoint has none. ALGORITHM is unknown: no preference/RL optimiser is named because no such stage exists; the card only inherits the base's gradient optimiser via "The model architecture and hyperparameters are the same as for [Lucie-7B](https://huggingface.co/OpenLLM-France/Lucie-7B) during the annealing phase" (i.e. AdamW, max LR 3e-5, batch size 1024), which is not an alignment algorithm in this schema's sense. VERSIONING: this checkpoint supersedes an earlier one — "It is meant to replace the original Lucie-7B-Instruct model that was released in January 2025" — so a roster row citing plain "Lucie-7B-Instruct" is a different artifact. SIBLING NOT IN THIS ROSTER: the paper names a second instruct variant, Lucie-7B-Instruct-human-data, trained on human-authored data only; if the roster ever needs a synthetic-vs-human SFT contrast within one lineage, that pair is available. CONTEXT: trained at 4096 tokens though the base is 32K, with a measured window of 22K — matters only if prompts are long. No card-vs-paper contradictions found.

BSC-LT/salamandra-7b-instruct.notes:
Single-stage SFT, not an instruct_bundle: the card documents exactly one post-training operation (instruction fine-tuning on 273k instructions) and explicitly denies a preference-optimisation stage, so there are no undocumented stages to bundle. Tooling, not an optimiser: "The instruction-tuned versions were produced with [FastChat](https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat)." FastChat is a training framework, so algorithm stays "unknown" — no named optimiser (DPO/PPO/GRPO/etc.) appears anywhere on the card.

DIRECTION, read carefully. The card says the model was NOT aligned through RLHF. That is an ABSENCE of safety alignment, not an inversion — no toxic-DPO, uncensoring or refusal-removal mixture is named, and every listed dataset (alpaca-cleaned, dolly, oasst2, open-orca, no-robots, tower-blocks, aya) is a standard instruction mixture. I therefore file direction "standard" while flagging that the checkpoint is explicitly un-safety-aligned, which matters for any analysis treating an instruct checkpoint as a superego layer: this one has no DPO/RLHF stage at all. Full disclaimer for context: "> It has been optimized to engage in conversation but has *NOT* been aligned through RLHF to filter or avoid sensitive topics.\n> As a result, it may generate harmful or inappropriate content.\n> The team is actively working to enhance its performance through further instruction and alignment with RL techniques."

REASONING rests partly on absence: the card never claims chain-of-thought or thinking capability, and states its purpose is instruction-following; the word "reasoning" occurs on the card only as an evaluation-benchmark category ("Commonsense Reasoning", the LLM-judge "reasoning_capability" rubric), never as a training target. I read that as "no", but the direct evidence is the proof-of-concept sentence quoted, not an explicit denial.

DATASETS quote is the card's "Finetuning Data" table, reproduced verbatim minus its header and total rows; the total row reads "| **Total**            | **35,444** | **183,265** | **40,638** | **1,622** | **702** | **11,198** | **272,869** |", which is where the 272,869 example count comes from.

NO CARD-VS-PAPER CONTRADICTION. The card points to the Salamandra Technical Report (arXiv:2502.08489), which corroborates both load-bearing fields — from-scratch pretraining ("The models were trained from scratch on highly multilingual data that comprises text in 35 European languages and code.") and the instruct variants as public-domain instruction fine-tunes ("Along with the base models, supplementary checkpoints that were fine-tuned on public-domain instruction data are also released for chat applications."), with the no-alignment point repeated in the introduction ("It is important to highlight that they have been optimized for dialogue use cases, but they are still unaligned with human preferences, which is something the team intends to address in future work."). The report abstract does not state the 12.875T figure; that number is card-only. The three report quotes are from the HF paper page rendering of arXiv:2502.08489, not from the PDF directly.

The instruct card's YAML `datasets:` list (togethercomputer/RedPajama-Data-1T, bigcode/starcoderdata, EleutherAI/the_pile_deduplicated, etc.) is inherited PRETRAINING data, not the finetuning mixture — the datasets claim above is sourced from the "Finetuning Data" table instead.

01-ai/Yi-1.5-9B-Chat.notes: STUB BY DUPLICATION. The Chat card is byte-identical to the base card — both 5,779 bytes, `diff` returns clean — so this repo carries no documentation of its own post-training whatsoever. Everything scorable comes from one family-level sentence that also sits on the base model. Confidence is low for that reason. METHOD: the only training statement is "fine-tuned on 3M diverse fine-tuning samples" — a single undifferentiated finetuning claim covering all Yi-1.5 chat models, with no stages broken out, so this is instruct_bundle rather than sft. BAAI/Aquila2-7B.notes:
CARD IS A STUB ON TRAINING. The whole card is a logo, a one-line series announcement, a June-2024 update note, an inference snippet and a licence line. It states only "Aquila2-7B is a base model that can be used for continuation." and defers everything else: "The additional details of the Aquila model will be presented in the official technical report. Please stay tuned for updates on official channels." It does not even cite the technical report (the chat card does). All training claims above come from the Aquila2 Technical Report (arXiv:2408.07410), not the card.

ON "independent". No source I could reach uses the phrase "from scratch" about Aquila2 -- the report uses that phrase only about a BASELINE, Baichuan2 ("They were trained from scratch on a massive dataset of 2.6 trillion tokens."). The from-scratch reading rests on three positive facts and one absence: (a) BAAI states it pre-trained the 7B on its own cluster (quoted above); (b) BAAI built the vocabulary itself -- "To identify the optimal vocabulary size, preliminary experiments were carried out with varying vocabulary sizes and language proportions. Based on the results, we decided to set Aquila2's vocabulary size at 100,000." -- and a bespoke vocabulary is incompatible with continuing another lab's checkpoint; (c) the LR/batch schedule starts from zero tokens -- "In the preliminary training phase encompassing the initial 8B tokens, the batch size is progressively elevated from 32 to 1024" and "The learning rate undergoes an initial escalation to 1.5 x 10-4 within the first 2B tokens, then decays to 1.5 x 10-5."; (d) no parent checkpoint is named anywhere in card, GitHub repo, or report. Judgement: independent, but on converging circumstantial evidence rather than an explicit sentence.

TOKEN COUNT -- DO NOT PROPAGATE 1.8T TO THE 7B. The report's only total is scoped to the 34B: "The Aquila-34B model was trained with a total of approximately 1.8 trillion bilingual Chinese and English tokens." Per-phase splits are likewise given only for 34B (523B/1053B/298B) and 70B (203B/719B/347B); the 7B is absent from that sentence. An appendix on data-recipe experiments mentions "Upon completion of training the 7B model on the v3 dataset (approximately 1000B tokens)" but that passage describes pilot runs used to select the data mixture, not the released checkpoint's total, so I am not booking it.

CORPUS-QUOTE HAZARD. The report also says "The training data corpus consists of an equal proportion of English and Chinese, sourced from WudaoCorpus [11] and Pile [12] for Chinese and English data, respectively." That sentence is in the Tokenizer subsection and describes the corpus used to FIT THE BPE VOCABULARY, not the model's pretraining mixture. It is easy to misfile as a datasets claim; I have not used it as one.

CARD-VS-PAPER CONTRADICTION ON THE HOSTED WEIGHTS. Paper, Table 1 ("The training configurations for the Aquila2 series models") lists Aquila2-7B with MaxLen 2048. Card, Updates 2024.6.6: "* The maximum processing length supported by the model has increased from 2048 to 8192" and "* Replaced tokenizer with higher compression ratio:" (a table showing Aquila2-original at 100k vocab and Aquila2-new at 143k). Live config.json confirms the card: vocab_size 143973, max_position_embeddings 8192. So the August-2024 report describes the SUPERSEDED 7B checkpoint; the weights currently served under this id are the June-2024 retokenized model, whose token count and data recipe are undocumented anywhere I could find. The report is the best available source for this id but is not strictly a document of the artefact you would download today.

The roster repo's card is HF-authored boilerplate: its only training statement is the heading "Model card for RWKV-4 | 7B parameters trained on Pile dataset" plus the YAML `datasets: EleutherAI/pile`. It documents architecture and usage snippets, nothing about the training run. Commit history shows the repo was created 2023-05-05 by `ybelkada` (Younes Belkada, Hugging Face) with commits "initial commit", "Upload RwkvForCausalLM", "Upload tokenizer", "Create README.md" -- i.e. this is a format conversion of BlinkDL's original .pth weights, not the training repo. `config.json` records `_name_or_path: /home/younes/rwkv/rwkv-4-7b-pile`, confirming a local conversion.

Same run, rounded differently (the paper's appendix notes the schedule takes 8043 mini-epochs for one pass over the Pile, matching the "8047" in the filename). Treat as ~330B.

WHICH FILE WAS CONVERTED IS NOT DOCUMENTED. BlinkDL's repo holds several 7B Pile checkpoints -- the 20221115 base, a ctx4096 context-extension finetune ("Fine-tuned to ctx_len 4096. * Likely the best. Please test."), and ctx8192 test builds. The HF conversion does not say which. `config.json` has `context_length: 1024`, consistent with the base ctx1024 checkpoint. Either way independence is unaffected: the ctx-extension finetunes are continued training of this same model on the same corpus, not derivation from another lab's checkpoint.

Independence is solid: the paper trains the whole 169M-14B ladder from scratch on the Pile, and the architecture (RWKV, an RNN) has no transformer checkpoint it could have been derived from.

RWKV/rwkv-raven-7b.notes:
THE ROSTER REPO'S OWN CARD DOCUMENTS NO TRAINING AT ALL. It is byte-for-byte the same boilerplate as rwkv-4-7b-pile except for the heading "Model card for RWKV-4 | 7B parameters chat version (Raven)" and one added line, "The "Raven" models needs to be prompted in a specific way, learn more about that [in the integration blogpost]" -- which is about prompting, not training. Every method/dataset claim above is sourced from the upstream BlinkDL repo, the HF integration blog, or the paper, not from this card. Hence confidence medium rather than high.

CARD-VS-CARD CONTRADICTION ON DATASETS. The RWKV/rwkv-raven-7b YAML declares `datasets:\n- EleutherAI/pile` -- inherited boilerplate copied from the base card. That names the PRETRAINING corpus of its base, not its post-training data; the repo names no SFT dataset. The upstream BlinkDL/rwkv-4-raven card names Alpaca/CodeAlpaca/Guanaco/GPT4All/ShareGPT, and the paper's ethics statement corroborates: "by building a series of LLMs trained on publicly released pretraining data (Gao et al., 2020; Biderman et al., 2022) and later fine-tuned on publicly available instructions (Taori et al., 2023; Chaudhary, 2023; Cheung, 2023; Anand et al., 2023; Anonymous, 2023; Yang, 2023; Ji et al., 2023a,b)." I have recorded the upstream/paper account, not the YAML.

DIRECTION IS GENUINELY UNRESOLVED, AND THIS IS THE ONE TO WATCH. No source describes Raven as uncensored or as refusal-removing, which would normally make it "standard". But the paper's bibliography entry for one of its cited SFT sources reads "Anonymous. 2023. Sharegpt_vicuna_unfiltered." -- the ShareGPT Vicuna *unfiltered* corpus, a variant built by stripping ChatGPT's refusals and moralising from the conversations. That is a de-censoring ingredient, cited by the model's own paper, in a mixture the card summarises only as "and more". It is one component of an otherwise ordinary instruction mixture, and the amount and the specific Raven build are undocumented, so I will not call the checkpoint "inverted" -- but neither can I certify "standard" from any source. Recorded as unknown deliberately.

VARIANT UNIDENTIFIED. BlinkDL's Raven repo held several language-ratio builds ("RWKV-4-Raven-Eng : 99% English + 1% Multilang", "RWKV-4-Raven-EngAndMore", "RWKV-4-Raven-ChnEng : 49% English + 50% Chinese + 1% Multilang", plus newer Eng99%-style names). The HF conversion (`_name_or_path: /home/younes/rwkv/rwkv-4-raven-7b`, created 2023-05-05) does not record which build or which date-stamped .pth it came from. If the roster treats this checkpoint's training mixture as known, that is over-claiming: the English/Chinese ratio alone varies from 99/0 to 49/50 across builds sharing this name.

No token or example count is stated for the fine-tuning anywhere in the card, the upstream card, the blog, or the paper.

On `reasoning`: recorded "no". The quote is the paper's own chain-of-thought evaluation of Raven -- CoT prompting was applied to it externally and it scored 5.43%, i.e. CoT is a probe of the model, not a training target. The SFT mixture is instruction data with no reasoning traces. No source claims CoT training.

google/gemma-2-9b.notes:
THE CARD AND THE PAPER DO NOT AGREE IN COVERAGE, AND THE GAP IS THE WHOLE FINDING. The HF card (card) describes pretraining purely as a token count over a three-category corpus and never once mentions distillation. The technical report (paper) states in its abstract: "We also train the 2B and 9B models with knowledge distillation (Hinton et al., 2015) instead of next token prediction." This is a silence in the card rather than a flat contradiction, but anyone auditing this lineage from the card alone would record it as an ordinary from-scratch pretraining run and would be wrong. The two sources agree exactly on the token count (8T), which is why confidence is high despite the gap.

On method="pretrain" rather than "distill": this checkpoint is the pretrained base variant and there is no post-training operation behind it, so under the field's own definition ("the post-training OPERATION that produced this checkpoint") pretrain is correct. I deliberately did NOT put "distill" in the method field, because that value would wrongly imply a post-training distillation of some released checkpoint. The distillation fact is carried by root.independent / root.derived_from instead. If your roster consumes only the method column it will miss the distillation entirely — this is a known limitation of filing it this way, flagged here on purpose.

released_base is "unknown", not "na" and not "no". It would be "na" for a plain root, but I have reported this root as derived, which makes the field meaningful. I cannot answer it: the teacher is never named, so nothing in the sources tells me whether it was released. "no" would have been a guess.

direction is "na": a pretrained base has no refusal behaviour to preserve or remove, so the axis is undefined. reasoning is "unknown" with an empty quote — no source addresses CoT-targeted training for the base. The card's line that mathematical text "helps the model learn logical reasoning" is about corpus composition, not chain-of-thought targeting, and I did not use it as evidence for that field.

THE METHOD FIELD LOSES A REAL STEP. allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-7B.notes:
INDEPENDENCE - the decisive field, and the card contains one sentence that can be misread as evidence of derivation. The card says: 'The training of our hybrid model makes use of Olmo 3 7B, except that we change the learning rate schedule to be a standard cosine schedule rather than the piecewise schedule used by Olmo 3. Additionally, we use the improved data mix of Olmo 3 32B instead of the Olmo 3 7B mix.' Read whole, that sentence is about the training CONFIGURATION (LR schedule, data mix) inherited from the Olmo 3 recipe, not about inheriting Olmo 3 weights. An automated summary of this page rendered it as 'Derived from another model / Base model: Olmo 3 7B'; that reading is not supported by the card text, and I flag it because it is the exact error a roster audit must not propagate. Evidence the run is a fresh pretraining, all from this card: (a) it has its own full three-stage pretraining pipeline with 'Stage 1: Initial Pretraining' at 5.50T tokens and 'Coverage: 97.53%+ of total pretraining budget'; (b) the architecture table gives it a peer 'Training Tokens' figure (5.50 Trillion) alongside Olmo 3 7B's 5.93 Trillion, i.e. a sibling run, not a delta; (c) the dimensions are incompatible with initialising from Olmo 3 7B - 'We reduced the number of heads from 32 to 30 while keeping the head dimension fixed at 128 (effectively reducing dmodel from 4096 to 3840).'; (d) pretraining-step checkpoints are released - 'For pretraining, the naming convention is `stage1-stepXXX`.'; (e) the abstract of the Olmo Hybrid paper (arXiv:2604.03444, 'Olmo Hybrid: From Theory to Practice and Back', Merrill et al., 3 Apr 2026, linked from the card) says 'Putting this theory to practice, we train Olmo Hybrid, a 7B-parameter model largely comparable to Olmo 3 7B but with the sliding window layers replaced by Gated DeltaNet layers.' and 'We show that Olmo Hybrid outperforms Olmo 3 across standard pretraining and mid-training evaluations, demonstrating the benefit of hybrid models in a controlled, large-scale setting.' - a controlled scaling comparison between two pretraining runs presupposes an independent run. Neither card nor paper abstract uses the literal phrase 'from scratch' or 'randomly initialized'; the judgement rests on the evidence above, not on a single quotable sentence. CARD-VS-PAPER, token count: card says '5.50 Trillion'; the paper HTML says 'we train Olmo Hybrid 7B on up to 6T tokens'. Card is the more specific and I report the card figure. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: 5.50T of a stated 5.50T+100B+50B total is 97.35%, not the '97.53%+' the card claims - a rounding or transcription slip, immaterial to independence. MERGE INSIDE PRETRAINING, worth knowing for any per-checkpoint statistic: '#### Model Merging
- 2 versions on 100B mix (midtraining), merged before starting long context run.' Both merged parents are this model's own mid-training runs, so this does not import an outside lineage, but the released base is a merge of two of its own branches rather than a single continuous run. ARCHITECTURE CAVEAT for anyone loading it: this is a hybrid RNN, not a plain transformer, and requires transformers>=5.3.0 ('Olmo Hybrid is supported in transformers 5.3.0 or higher'); note the Model Description field nonetheless states 'Model type: a Transformer style autoregressive language model.', contradicting the card's own architecture section. reasoning=unknown rather than na because the field enum has no na; the card says nothing about chain-of-thought for the base, though the stage 2 mix is '8% thinking' data. released_base=na and direction=na are definitional for a pretrained root, hence empty quotes.

This card's 'Model Details' training section is byte-identical to the DPO card's and documents BOTH stages: it lists '#### Stage 1: SFT' AND '#### Stage 2:DPO' (typo, no space after the colon, preserved). Taken alone, the prose does not establish that THIS checkpoint stops after SFT - it reads as a description of the whole Instruct pipeline, pasted onto both repos. What does establish it, independent of the name (rule 3): the release table on this same card places this exact id in the SFT row and a different id in the DPO row - the '**SFT**' row ends '| [Olmo-Hybrid-Instruct-SFT-7B](https://huggingface.co/allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-Instruct-SFT-7B) |' while the '**DPO**' row ends '| [Olmo-Hybrid-Instruct-DPO-7B](https://huggingface.co/allenai/Olmo-Hybrid-Instruct-DPO-7B) |'. So method=sft is sound, but it is sound on the metadata and the stage table, not on the prose. REASONING CONTRADICTION, why I return unknown rather than 'no': the release table separates an 'Olmo Hybrid Think 7B' column (the reasoning branch) from the 'Olmo Hybrid Instruct 7B' column that contains this checkpoint, which implies non-reasoning; but the card's own inference example prints a chain-of-thought opener - ">> '<think>Okay, so the question is who would win in a fight...'" - and the recommended max_tokens is 32768. That example is very likely copy-pasted from the Think card, but I will not adjudicate a card against itself, so the field stays unknown. DIRECTION: no sentence on this card states a safety or refusal posture, and the eval table's 'Safety' row is blank for both Hybrid columns while populated for the Olmo 3 columns (89.2 / 90.2). I record 'standard' on the strength of the mixture description quoted - a conventional math/code/chat/general-knowledge instruction mixture with no de-censoring or toxic-DPO component named anywhere - but flag that this is inferred from what the mixture IS, not from any explicit statement, and that no safety evaluation was published for this checkpoint. ALGORITHM: no optimiser is named distinct from the operation. The paper says only 'As a proof of concept, we also apply the Olmo 3 post-training recipe to Olmo Hybrid'; that points at the Olmo 3 recipe but does not itself name the variant, and I did not transfer Olmo 3's DPO variant onto this row. train_tokens: no token or example count for post-training appears on the card. PKU-Alignment/beaver-7b-v1.0.notes: METHOD/ALGORITHM SPLIT MATTERS HERE. The operation is RLHF (Safe RLHF); the optimiser is PPO under a Lagrangian constraint -- a roster recording only 'rlhf' cannot distinguish this from a plain-PPO or DPO run. Paper abstract: 'We formalize the safety concern of LLMs as an optimization task of maximizing the reward function while satisfying specified cost constraints. Leveraging the Lagrangian method to solve this constrained problem, Safe RLHF dynamically adjusts the balance between the two objectives during fine-tuning.' The paper does NOT contain the string 'PPO-Lagrangian' anywhere (0 occurrences); it names PPO for the RL phase and the Lagrangian method for the constraint, so I recorded exactly that and did not import the commoner 'PPO-Lag' label from elsewhere. v1.0 IS ROUND 1 OF 3, WHICH AFFECTS UNIT COUNTING: the paper describes 'a three-round fine-tuning using Safe RLHF' and evaluates 'models from three iterations of Safe RLHF: Beaver-v1 , Beaver-v2 , and Beaver-v3'. beaver-7b-v2.0 and v3.0 are successive iterations built ON TOP of v1.0, so if the roster carries them they are descendants, not siblings, and treating them as independent observations would double- or triple-count this one lineage. Safe RLHF also trains separate reward and cost models, released as beaver-7b-v1.0-reward and -cost; those are auxiliary models, not policy checkpoints. TRAIN_TOKENS unknown: neither the card nor the paper abstract gives a count for round 1 specifically. The safe-rlhf GitHub describes the PKU-SafeRLHF DATASET as having 'over 300k examples', but that is the dataset's total size, not v1.0's round-1 training set, so I did not record it as this checkpoint's train_tokens. TYPO PRESERVED in the method quote: the card writes 'Standord Alpaca', not 'Stanford'. LICENCE CONFLICT, card vs repo: the CARD says 'Non-commercial license' for the model, while the safe-rlhf GITHUB README says 'Safe-RLHF is released under Apache License 2.0'. I still score method 'pretrain' and independent 'yes' because initialisation is from scratch and the distillation is a supervision signal, not a weight inheritance - but a roster that treats distillation as derivation should flag this row rather than accept it silently.

DO NOT MISREAD THE ARCHITECTURE TAG. config.json gives architectures ['Qwen3ForCausalLM'], model_type 'qwen3', and HF auto-tags the repo 'qwen3'. CARD IS THIN, BLOG IS NOT. The card alone would support only method/license/direction; every token count, the optimiser, and the distillation stage come from the linked blog. kakaocorp/kanana-2-3b-instruct.notes:
WHY instruct_bundle AND NOT sft/rlvr/merge. One checkpoint absorbs four operations and no intermediate is released: staged SFT -> per-domain RL (DAPO) producing domain experts -> SCE weight merge -> calibration. The blog's own Table 5 ('표 5. Kanana-2-3B-Instruct 모델의 학습 단계별 성능 변화') scores three of those stages separately (SFT avg 46.18, Merge 50.95, Calibration 51.52) - the stages are DOCUMENTED but not RELEASED, so a roster cannot address them as separate checkpoints. 'merge' is a defensible alternative coding for the final operation; I chose instruct_bundle because it covers what the released weights actually contain. Merge quote: '모델의 가중치들을 병합할 때에는 각 Domain Expert 모델들의 고유 강점을 간섭 현상 없이 융화하기 위해 SCE (Select, Calculate, Erase) 방식을 사용하였습니다.' Staged SFT quote: '이를 완화하기 위해 초반에 적은 비중의 Tool Call 데이터로 시작하여 점차 비중을 높여가는 Staged SFT 방식을 적용하였습니다.'

CARD vs BLOG (not a contradiction, a resolution gap). The card says only: 'Kanana-2-3B was **pretrained from scratch on TPU clusters** and further improved through post-training with **supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning**, resulting in strong instruction-following and reasoning capabilities.' It names no optimiser. The blog names DAPO and rejects GRPO. A card-only audit would record algorithm 'unknown' here and would be unable to distinguish this checkpoint from any other SFT+RL model - exactly the Tulu-3 vs Tulu-3.1 failure the schema guards against.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IN THE BLOG (verbatim, typo included): '이렇게 SFT가 완료된 모델로부터 위에 기술한 5개의 Domain((Instruction Following, Math, Code, Tool, Chat, Knowledge) Expert를 얻기 위한 RL 학습을 진행하였습니다.' It says FIVE domains and then lists SIX (and the earlier pipeline sentence lists a different five: Chat, Math, Code, Tool Call, Instruction Following - no Knowledge). Table 5 has six domain columns including Knowledge. So the count '5' is wrong; six is what was actually run.

reasoning = unknown, deliberately. No thinking/CoT mode, no reasoning-trace training, and no <think> template is documented anywhere. The card's phrase 'strong instruction-following and reasoning capabilities' is a capability claim, not evidence of CoT targeting, so I did not file it as support. Weak contrary evidence: for the BASE distillation Kakao tested Base/Instruct/Thinking teachers and picked the Instruct one ('그 결과, 학습 과정 전반에 걸쳐 Instruct 모델을 Teacher로 사용할 때 가장 우수한 성능을 보임을 확인했습니다.'), i.e. the thinking teacher was explicitly not selected. Benchmarks reported as '-CoT' (MMLU-CoT etc.) are eval prompting formats, not training.

direction = unknown, deliberately. Neither source says anything about refusals, safety data, censoring or de-censoring - there is no safety section at all. Nothing suggests inversion and 'standard' is almost certainly right in practice, but I found no sentence that supports 'standard' for THIS checkpoint, so I am not attaching one. Treat as a documentation gap, not as a de-censored model.

train_tokens = unknown, deliberately. No post-training token or example count is given for the 3B. The blog's 300B-token figure ('2B, 1.3B, 0.9B 각 단계는 각각 300B 토큰 규모로 Distillation을 수행했습니다') belongs to the 1.3B/0.9B compression models and must NOT be copied onto this row. Only a 32K sequence-packing detail is stated for SFT.

Related but out of scope: the 1.3B/0.9B siblings use a different recipe again - off-policy distillation then 'RLVR 및 Generative reward model' multi-domain RL, because Parallel-RL was unstable at that size. Do not generalise this row's DAPO coding to them.

microsoft/phi-4-reasoning.notes:
CARD-VS-PAPER CONTRADICTION ON METHOD, and it is the load-bearing one. The HF card's Description says this checkpoint was 'finetuned from Phi-4 using supervised fine-tuning on a dataset of chain-of-thought traces and reinforcement learning' — SFT *and* RL. The technical report (arXiv:2504.21318) assigns the RL to a DIFFERENT checkpoint: 'Trained via supervised fine-tuning of Phi-4 on carefully curated set of "teachable" prompts...' for this model, and then 'We further develop Phi-4-reasoning-plus, a variant enhanced through a short phase of outcome-based reinforcement learning that offers higher performance by generating longer reasoning traces.' The card is the loose source: its Description paragraph reads as boilerplate shared across the Phi-4-reasoning family, while the paper distinguishes the two releases explicitly. I recorded method 'sft' on the paper's authority, and flag that a roster taking the card at face value would wrongly record RL for this checkpoint. Conservative assignment: 'sft' for phi-4-reasoning, RL only for Phi-4-reasoning-plus.

METHOD ALTERNATIVE — 'distill'. The paper states the SFT targets were 'reasoning demonstrations generated using o3-mini', i.e. distillation from a closed OpenAI model. I filed 'sft' because that is the operation both sources name, but a roster whose 'distill' category means 'trained on another model's generations' has a legitimate claim on this checkpoint, and the quote supports either reading. Flagging rather than choosing silently. This also creates a cross-lab dependence: the reasoning behaviour is inherited from o3-mini, so the checkpoint is not behaviourally independent of OpenAI's model even though its weights descend only from phi-4.

ALGORITHM IS GENUINELY UNSOURCED. The card says 'reinforcement learning' and the paper says 'outcome-based reinforcement learning' (of -plus), but neither the card nor the abstract names an optimiser — no GRPO, no PPO. I did not read the full PDF body, which may name one. Recorded 'unknown' with an empty quote rather than guessing GRPO from the era.

REPO CASE. The canonical repo is microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning (capital P) — the card's own license_link resolves to that path. The roster id microsoft/phi-4-reasoning reaches it via HuggingFace's case-insensitive redirect. Not a stub, not withdrawn: live and fully documented.

RELEASED_BASE 'yes' on strong grounds: microsoft/phi-4 is a public HF repo under MIT, and I fetched its card directly for the 9.8T pretraining figure.

The DIRECTION quote is about alignment/safety data in the SFT mixture, which is what makes it 'standard' rather than 'inverted' — a safety-added model, not an uncensored one.

LAB COUNTRY IS NOT CARD-SOURCED. The card names 'Microsoft Research' as Developers; it states no headquarters. 'United States' is general knowledge, not evidence from the source, and the lab quote supports only the org name.

Search budget note: WebSearch was exhausted for this session, so all findings come from three primary fetches (the phi-4-reasoning card, the phi-4 card, the arXiv abstract). The full paper PDF body was not read; the SFT example count and the RL optimiser name are the two fields most likely recoverable there.

METHOD CHOICE: 'instruct_bundle' rather than 'dpo' because only one artefact was released; the report documents the stages (SFT, DPO on PTS pairs, judge-guided DPO) but no per-stage checkpoint exists to attach them to. The terminal operation is judge-guided DPO.

Round 1 mixture (Table 7) sums to ~250k samples: unknown + safety data 3,000; generic multiple-choice Q&A 132,859; math data 76,552; python data 16,080; cpp, go, java, js, rust data 21,806. Table 8 (judge-guided DPO) lists: unknown + safety data 43,842; any vs any overall 266,000; any vs any accuracy 532,000.

CARD vs REPORT CONTRADICTION on pretraining tokens. Card: '| **Training data**       | 9.8T tokens'. Report: 'The model was pretrained for approximately 10T tokens'. The card figure is the specific one, the report rounds. Not material, but recorded.

REASONING - TENSION, not contradiction. Scored 'no' because phi-4 is a standard chat assistant with no separate reasoning/think channel, and Microsoft's own later release treats CoT training as the thing that had to be added on top ('finetuned from Phi-4 using supervised fine-tuning on a dataset of chain-of-thought traces'). Against this, the phi-4 report does invoke CoT in its data principles and limitations: 'Chain-of-Thought: Data should encourage systematic reasoning, teaching the model various approaches to the problems in a step-by-step manner.' and 'Moreover, as our data contains a lot of chain-of-thought examples, phi-4 sometimes gives long elaborate answers even for simple problems'. NOT DERIVED - the evidence. The report says 'The architecture closely follows phi-3-medium, except that we now use the tiktoken tokenizer (for better multilingual support) with a padded vocabulary size of 100,352 (including unused tokens) and we use full attention over the 4K context length, rather than a 2K sliding window used in phi-3-medium.' The card's 'Our training data is an extension of the data used for Phi-3' is a DATA statement, not weight inheritance, and must not be read as continual pretraining. The card's compute line ('| **GPUs** | 1920 H100-80G', '| **Training time** | 21 days') is consistent with a full from-scratch run at this token count. The abstract's 'previous models in the Phi family largely distill the capabilities of a teacher model (specifically GPT-4)' concerns synthetic data generation, not weight distillation, and it says phi-4 goes 'beyond distillation'. microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus.notes:
CARD-VS-PAPER DISAGREEMENT ON THIS CHECKPOINT'S OPERATION, and it changes the method value. The HF card presents SFT and RL as one undifferentiated description of the released model: 'Phi-4-reasoning-plus is a state-of-the-art open-weight reasoning model finetuned from Phi-4 using supervised fine-tuning on a dataset of chain-of-thought traces and reinforcement learning.' On the card alone the correct value is instruct_bundle. The technical report (arXiv:2504.21318, same authors, same release day) separates the stages: SFT of phi-4 produced Phi-4-reasoning, and this checkpoint is the RL step on top of it — section 4 is titled 'Phi-4-reasoning-plus: A bit of RL on top of Phi-4-reasoning'. I scored method from the report, so the value is rlvr, not instruct_bundle. The card alone does not get you there.

WHY rlvr AND NOT rlhf/ppo/dpo: the reward is rule-based over verifiable math answers, not a learned preference model — 'We employ a rule-based reward model to avoid complexities and potential reward hacking associated with neu[ral reward models]' — and the report's intro calls the RL set 'high-quality math-focused problems with verifiable solutions'. RL was math-only: 'The RL training focused exclusively on mathematical reasoning' and 'the seed data contained no coding exercises'.

BASE-MODEL AMBIGUITY, does not change released_base: the HF frontmatter declares base_model: microsoft/phi-4, while the report says the RL ran on Phi-4-reasoning. Both are released public repos (HF API returned 200 for microsoft/phi-4, microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning and microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus on 2026-08-15), so released_base is yes under either reading. But a roster that records 'trained from microsoft/phi-4' off the frontmatter is recording the card's claim, not the report's, and silently drops the intermediate SFT checkpoint.

TRAIN_TOKENS: the two claims are different stages, not a contradiction. The card's '16B tokens' is the SFT mixture ('The final model was trained for 16B tokens using this mixture', report S3.2); the RL stage is measured in problems, not tokens — 6,400 actually trained on, from a 72,401-problem seed pool, rounded to '~6K' in the report intro. No token count is published for the RL stage.

DIRECTION: standard, and the evidence is affirmative rather than a mere absence — safety post-training was added (safety SFT to Microsoft guidelines, Microsoft AI Red Team evaluation, Toxigen). Nothing in card or report describes refusal removal or de-censoring.

COMPUTE, for context: 32 H100-80G for 2.5 days, training dates January 2025 - April 2025, released 30 April 2025. 14B params, 32k context. Card notes it generates ~50% more tokens than Phi-4-reasoning, the known RL side effect.

LAB COUNTRY IS INFERRED, NOT SOURCED. The card says only 'Microsoft Research'; the report's affiliation line says only 'Microsoft'. Neither names a country. 'United States' comes from Microsoft Corporation being headquartered in Redmond, Washington — background knowledge, no quote. The MIT LICENSE file's 'Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation.' establishes the legal entity but not the jurisdiction. Treat the country field as unquoted.

SCOPE WARNING RELEVANT TO THIS PROJECT: the card states 'This model is designed and tested for math reasoning only.' Post-training covered math/code/STEM/safety; a logit battery over sexual, violent or profane prompts is far outside the documented domain for this checkpoint.

CARD IS SILENT ON TRAINING AND IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE BASE CARD. I downloaded both raw READMEs; apart from which table row is bolded, they are the same file. Neither names a base_model, neither says SFT/DPO/PPO, neither lists a dataset. Confidence low per the audit rule. The card contains no SFT statement. Do not let that phrasing enter the roster.

WHY instruct_bundle. The stages ARE documented in the blog (SFT, then reinforcement learning), but only one artifact was released for this tier — there is no separate SFT or DPO checkpoint for kanana-1.5-8b — so the released checkpoint bundles the whole post-training recipe. The blog's three headline changes for 1.5 are: (1) on-policy RL introduced, (2) scalar reward model replaced by a generative reward model, (3) combination with a verifiable reward function. Supporting quotes, kept out of the field claims because they support the pipeline description rather than any single enum field: "이런 문제들을 해결하는 방법으로 Kanana 1.5에서는 generative reward model을 도입하게 되었습니다." and "이런 영역들에 대해서는 generative reward model의 예측이 부족하다고 판단하여 Kanana 1.5에서는 추가적으로 verifiable function을 도입하였습니다."

METHOD AMBIGUITY WORTH RECORDING. Because the RL stage uses a learned generative reward model AND a verifiable reward function, this checkpoint is a hybrid of what the schema separates as rlhf and rlvr. A roster that forces a single value will lose that. The algorithm field (PPO) is the discriminating fact and is cleanly sourced.

GENERATION CHANGE FROM 1.0 IS EXPLICIT, AND THIS IS A CONTRADICTION TRAP. The technical report describes the Kanana 1.0 pipeline as SFT -> offline DPO -> online DPO: "The process begins with offline preference optimization (Meng et al. 2024; Jung et al. 2024), where we apply direct preference optimization (DPO) (Rafailov et al. 2023) using the offline preference data." The blog explicitly repudiates that for 1.5, describing the DPO pipeline in the past tense as what the March report showed — "지난 3월에 발표된 Kanana 테크리포트의 내용을 보면 기존에는 SFT 이후 Offline Direct Preference Optimization(DPO) 와 Online DPO 이렇게 두번의 Preference alignment 과정을 적용한것을 확인하실 수 있습니다." — before announcing the move to PPO. Anyone sourcing this checkpoint from the arXiv report alone would record DPO/online DPO and be WRONG for the 1.5 release. The report is also the wrong scope in a second way: it contains no 8B instruct model at all (its post-training tables cover 2.1B/9.8B/32.5B only; the card's "Kanana-8B" instruct row, MT-Bench 7.13 / IFEval 76.91, appears nowhere in the paper).

DIRECTION EVIDENCE IS 1.0-VINTAGE. The only safety-data statement I could source is the Kanana 1.0 SFT mixture (96K safety instances covering ethics, privacy, toxicity, bias). The 1.5 blog does not restate a safety component. Direction "standard" is therefore sourced one generation back; nothing anywhere suggests an inverted/de-censoring mixture, and Kakao separately ships kanana-safeguard-8b / kanana-safeguard-siren-8b guardrail models.

released_base=yes: neither card declares a base_model, so the base->instruct link is inferential from the blog naming "Kanana-1.5-8B의 base, instruct" as jointly trained and jointly released under Apache 2.0, plus the base repo existing publicly. There is no explicit "trained from kakaocorp/kanana-1.5-8b-base" sentence anywhere I found.

allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT-no-safet.notes: STUB — and this is the most important negative finding in the audit. The card is the unedited HuggingFace auto-generated template: every field reads "[More Information Needed]", including Developed by, Model type, License, Finetuned from model, Training Data, and Citation. Its only self-description is "This is the model card of a 🤗 transformers model that has been pushed on the Hub. This model card has been automatically generated." The YAML frontmatter is only "library_name: transformers" and "tags: []" — no license, no base_model. I confirmed via the HF API that repo metadata carries no license and no base_model either, and the sole arXiv tag is arxiv:1910.09700, which is the boilerplate carbon-emissions citation from the template, NOT the Tulu 3 paper. DECISIVE CHECK: I downloaded all four *-no-*-data cards and they are byte-identical (md5 39727e7063aa6976a8c044d325155bd1, 5174 bytes each). A single template was pushed to all four repos. Therefore the card provides NO evidence of what was ablated, what the base was, or that SFT was the operation — everything here would be inferred from the repo NAME alone, which rule 3 forbids. The Tulu 3 paper does describe SFT data-mixture ablations, but nothing in this repo points to that paper, and no artifact ties this specific checkpoint to a specific ablation arm. If the roster's safety-ablation results depend on this checkpoint being the no-safety arm, that identification currently rests on the repo name and on Ai2's upload timestamps (2024-12-14, within six minutes across the four repos), not on any documentation.

NousResearch/Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B.notes: The MODEL CARD never names SFT or DPO — on the card alone method would be unknown. All method/algorithm/token/direction claims here come from the Hermes 3 Technical Report (arXiv:2408.11857), which the card explicitly points to. I string-matched every quote against the raw arXiv HTML. METHOD CHOICE: the released checkpoint is the product of SFT followed by a LoRA-adapter DPO stage; the report documents the two stages in separate sections (4.1 SFT, 4.2 DPO) but only one checkpoint is released, so I record the FINAL operation (dpo) rather than instruct_bundle. If the roster's convention is that a single checkpoint bundling SFT+DPO with no separate SFT release should be instruct_bundle, reclassify — the evidence supports either reading and the distinction is a convention, not a fact. DIRECTION: I have recorded "inverted", but flag the interpretive step honestly. The report never says it removed refusal data or used a toxic-DPO mixture; what it says is that the training data was built to make the model comply neutrally rather than refuse, and that guardrails belong at the system level, not in the weights: "We believe that a more appropriate place for guardrails and active intervention is at the larger system levels, rather than on the models themselves, which can result in an a priori lobotomization of potential lines of thinking. For Hermes, there is no such thing as latent thoughtcrime." The abstract's term is "a neutrally-aligned generalist instruct and tool use model". If the roster reserves "inverted" strictly for explicit de-censoring mixtures, this should be "standard" or "unknown". LICENSE ODDITY: frontmatter reads "license: llama3", not llama3.1, although the model is a Llama 3.1 derivative — quoted exactly as written. The card's base_model field names "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B", the root repo's former name.

Every claim above that comes from the card is a family-level statement I have matched to this checkpoint via the card's own download table row. Not a stub, but not checkpoint-specific either.

BASE MODEL — the headline finding. The roster places this under Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B; both primary sources say Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B. Card table row: "| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B  | [Qwen2.5-Math-7B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B) | [🤗 HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B)   |". Weight-level corroboration: this repo's config.json has rope_theta 10000 and sliding_window 4096 (matching Qwen2.5-Math-7B) where Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B has rope_theta 1000000.0 and sliding_window 131072. direction "unknown" is deliberate. Nothing in the card or the paper states a direction for the DISTILLED checkpoints. The paper's helpfulness/harmlessness language ("a secondary reinforcement learning stage aimed at improving the model's helpfulness and harmlessness") describes R1's own second RL stage, not the distills, which received only SFT on R1 outputs. Attaching that quote here would be exactly the misfiling rule 1 warns about. There is no evidence of a de-censoring or refusal-removal objective either — absence of that evidence is not a finding.

The card asserts MIT for the released artifact and acknowledges the upstream Apache-2.0 provenance; it does not resolve which governs a downstream user.

allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125.notes:
THE INDEPENDENCE FINDING. The card calls this model "an improved version of OLMoE-09-24" and says main was "annealed from `step1200000-tokens5033B`" — but that branch does not exist in THIS repo. Repo-structure evidence (HF refs API): allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125 has 16 branches, ALL of the form stage2-ingredient{1,2,3}-step*-tokens* topping out at 101B tokens; there is no stage-1 branch. allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 has 246 branches carrying the full stage-1 trajectory including step1200000-tokens5033B, plus only main and fp32 beyond it. Conclusion: 0125 = the 0924 stage-1 pretraining trunk + a NEW ~101B-token stage-2 anneal on dolmino-mix-1124 (three candidate 'ingredients' were released; the 0924 anneal was the same 23,842 steps on a different mix). Both cards carry word-for-word identical branch text, which is why this is easy to miss. released_base is 'yes' not 'na' precisely because the checkpoint it was annealed from IS publicly released — as a branch of the 0924 repo.

UNRESOLVED: the card defers to "the [paper appendix](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02060) for details", but I could not find any mention of 0125, January 2025, or dolmino in arXiv:2409.02060 (abstract page and v2 PDF both checked; PDF text extraction was partial, so this is a failure to confirm, not a confirmed absence).

CONTRADICTION (card vs its own siblings): this base card's link block describes the adaptation recipe as "**SFT** ... [Data](https://hf.co/datasets/allenai/tulu-v3.1-mix-preview-4096-OLMoE)" and "**DPO/KTO (Direct Preference Optimization/Kahneman-Tversky Optimization)**, [Checkpoints](https://huggingface.co/allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct), [Preference Data](https://hf.co/datasets/allenai/ultrafeedback_binarized_cleaned)". The four stage cards instead name tulu-3-sft-olmo-2-mixture, olmoe-0125-1b-7b-preference-mix and RLVR-GSM, treat DPO and Instruct as separate checkpoints, and never mention KTO. The base card's block is 0924-era text carried over (it also links the 0924 wandb logs); the stage cards are the better source for the 0125 recipe.

reasoning: no card text addresses chain-of-thought training, so 'unknown' rather than 'no'. direction is 'na': pretraining/annealing stage, no refusal training defined.

allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct.notes:
READ THE ALGORITHM CLAIM'S SCOPE BEFORE USING IT. The Instruct card names the OPERATION (RLVR) but NEVER names an optimiser. My PPO quote is from the Tülu 3 paper (arXiv:2411.15124, Table 21 caption), which the card explicitly points to ("Check out the OLMoE paper or Tülu 3 paper for more details!"), and it does tie PPO specifically to "optimizing against the verifiable reward function" — i.e. to RLVR, not merely to preference tuning. But it is a RECIPE-LEVEL statement about Tülu 3, not a checkpoint-level statement about OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct. Treat as inherited-recipe evidence, downgrade if the roster needs checkpoint-level attestation. This is exactly the Tulu-3-PPO vs Tulu-3.1-GRPO distinction the field exists to capture, which is why I sourced it rather than leaving it unknown — but it is not from the card.

CROSS-CARD CONTRADICTION on the DPO stage. This card says the upstream DPO used "[this dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/olmo-2-1124-13b-preference-mix)". The DPO card says "further DPO training on [this dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/olmoe-0125-1b-7b-preference-mix)". The DPO card is more credible: its named mix is OLMoE-specific, built from prompt subsets suffixed _olmoe_1b-7b (e.g. "ai2-adapt-dev/sft_v3.9_used_on_policy_p0_olmoe_1b-7b"), whereas olmo-2-1124-13b-preference-mix is the OLMo-2-13B artefact — almost certainly pasted from that model's card. Hence confidence 'medium' for this checkpoint: its own RLVR claims are clean, but its account of its own ancestry is demonstrably sloppy.

The stage table labels this checkpoint "**Final Models (RLVR)**", consistent with method=rlvr rather than instruct_bundle: the stages ARE documented separately across four cards, so rule 5 does not apply here.

Same caveats as above on train_tokens (dataset size, and 7,473 prompts under RL is episodes-not-tokens — the Tülu 3 paper's PPO table quotes 'Total Episodes' in the 100,000–300,000 range for its own runs) and on direction.

allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B.notes:
INDEPENDENCE: yes, high confidence. The card carries NO `base_model` field in its YAML frontmatter (frontmatter is: license, language, library_name, datasets: allenai/dolma3_mix-5.5T-1125, model-index), and the body documents a from-scratch staged pretraining run beginning at 'Stage 1: Initial Pretraining' on 5.50T tokens of dolma3_mix-5.5T-1125. Nothing on the card describes pruning, depth-upscaling, distillation, or continued pretraining from another party's checkpoint. It also releases its own pretraining-step checkpoints ('For pretraining, the naming convention is `stage1-stepXXX`'), which only a from-scratch run has. This lineage counts as an INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION.

ONE THING THAT COULD BE MISREAD AS DERIVATION, and is not: the card contains a '#### Model Merging' section reading '- 7B Model: No merging' and '- 32B Model: 2 versions on 100B mix, merged before starting long context run.  Final checkpoint is merged 4 final checkpoints.' (double space after 'run.' is in the original). This is a self-merge of Ai2's OWN checkpoints from within this same pretraining run — a soup over mid-training ingredients — not a merge with any external model. It does not make the root derived, but a roster that classifies by keyword would wrongly file this model as method 'merge'. Method is 'pretrain'.

allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct.notes:
METHOD: rlvr, not instruct_bundle. Although the model is named '-Instruct', this card documents its stage: the release table places this exact id in the 'Final Models (RLVR)' row, YAML base_model = allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-DPO (so SFT and DPO are separate released checkpoints, not folded into this one), YAML datasets = allenai/Dolci-Instruct-RL, and the body describes '#### Stage 3: RLVR / - reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards on the Dolci-Think-RL-7B dataset.' A fourth corroboration is this card's unique addition, absent from the SFT and DPO cards: '**NOTE**: For this model, due to a checkpointing issue, we only are releasing the final few checkpoints. See our other RL jobs for more detailed intermediate checkpoint suite.' — that references an RL job for this specific model. instruct_bundle would be wrong here because the stages ARE released and documented separately.

ALGORITHM: unknown. This is the field most at risk of being guessed. The card names the operation (reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards) but no optimiser. Fetches of the Olmo 3 paper (arXiv:2512.13961) surfaced the system name 'OlmoRL' and returned no occurrence of GRPO, PPO, or 'policy optimization' in the retrieved text; further, the OlmoRL sentence returned concerns Olmo 3.1 Think 32B, a different branch from this Instruct model. I could not re-verify those strings character-for-character, so I file no algorithm claim and no paper quote. If the roster needs the optimiser, it must come from the paper PDF section 4.4 or the open-instruct training config, neither of which I read.

reasoning=no is an INFERENCE about the Instruct branch, and the card is not clean on it. Support: the release table gives Instruct and Think as separate columns, this id sits in the Instruct column, and the sentence I quote attributes long chain-of-thought to the Think variants. Against: the templated body says training used Dolci-Think-SFT/DPO/RL-7B datasets, which would imply thinking data. I read the '-7B' Think dataset names as copy-paste from the 7B Think card and the frontmatter's Dolci-Instruct-RL as authoritative, but a reader who weighs the body over the frontmatter could reach 'yes'. Treat this one field as medium confidence; the eval table also shows this checkpoint at AIME 2024 67.8 and AIME 2025 57.9, which is high for a non-thinking model and is worth resolving against the paper before the roster relies on reasoning=no.

No token or example counts on the card. This card carries the arXiv citation @misc{olmo2025olmo3, eprint 2512.13961. Not a stub.

The technical report assigns the four-stage process (Long-CoT Cold Start → Reasoning RL → Thinking Mode Fusion → General RL) to the flagship models only, and explicitly places the 8B in the strong-to-weak distillation track alongside 0.6B/1.7B/4B/14B/30B-A3B. Its method is distill (off-policy on teacher outputs, then on-policy logit/KL alignment against Qwen3-32B or Qwen3-235B-A22B). A roster that codes Qwen3-8B as RLVR or GRPO from the family paper would be wrong at the checkpoint level.

The lineage therefore descends from Yi (3.1T tokens, 01.AI), and Yi's own 9B was itself continual pretraining from Yi-6B ("Yi-9B is continuously trained based on Yi-6B, using 0.8T tokens"). For roster statistics this lineage should NOT be counted as an independent observation at the pretraining level — it shares its pretraining run with the whole Yi family. The arithmetic corroborates the derivation: Yi's 3.1T + Yi-1.5's 500B = 3.6T, exactly the card's cumulative figure. Aleph-Alpha/Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control-hf.summary: One lineage, one lab, fully in-house. Aleph Alpha Research pretrained a 7B decoder-only transformer FROM RANDOM INITIALIZATION on ~7.7T tokens (4.7T + 3T, two curriculum steps), then instruction-tuned it into Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control (SFT), then applied DPO for helpfulness and safety to produce Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control-aligned. CRITICAL CAVEAT FOR THE ROSTER: the declared lineage root, Pharia-1-LLM-7B-control-hf, is NOT a base model — the card calls it "a fine-tuned small model" and describes full-model instruction fine-tuning on it. The actual pretrained model both checkpoints descend from was never released (the Aleph-Alpha HF org listing has no raw Pharia-1-LLM-7B base; only control, control-aligned and their -hf conversions). So this lineage supplies a clean SFT -> DPO pair but NO base layer. Any base->SFT or base->superego statistic computed with control-hf standing in for the base is measuring an SFT checkpoint against its own DPO child, not a pretraining->alignment contrast.

Section 3.2 gives the distillation objective but never names or sizes the production teacher; the only concrete teacher sizes I found (7B, 27B) appear in an ablation table, which is a different setting and which I am NOT treating as the identity of the production 9B teacher. google/gemma-2-9b.summary: google/gemma-2-9b (root, Google) → google/gemma-2-9b-it (instruction-tuned). Two checkpoints, both live and readable on HF but gated behind Google's licence acceptance (the rendered pages fetch fine; https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-9b/raw/main/README.md returns HTTP 401). THE CRITICAL FINDING IS ABOUT THE ROOT AND IT IS NOT ON THE MODEL CARD. The Gemma 2 technical report (arXiv:2408.00118) states in its abstract that the 9B was trained by knowledge distillation from a teacher rather than by next-token prediction: "We also train the 2B and 9B models with knowledge distillation (Hinton et al., 2015) instead of next token prediction." The HF card for google/gemma-2-9b never mentions distillation at all — it reports only the 8T token count and the corpus categories. Since the task's definition of DERIVED explicitly includes "distilled", I have set root.independent = "no". Read the nuance in root.derived_from and the notes before using this in the statistics: the 9B's weights are NOT initialised from another checkpoint and it is a full 8-trillion-token pretraining run of its own, so it is not derived in the pruned/upscaled/continued-pretraining sense; what is inherited is the training SIGNAL, from a teacher the report never names. Whether that counts as a dependent observation for your roster hinges on whether the (unnamed) teacher or its siblings — notably google/gemma-2-27b, which the report says was trained on 13T tokens by ordinary next-token prediction — also appear in the roster. If the roster contains no other Gemma-2 lineage, treating this as one independent pretraining run is defensible; if it contains gemma-2-27b, it is not. I could not resolve the teacher's identity from the primary source and did not guess. Post-training for the -it checkpoint is documented ONLY in the paper (SFT → RLHF → model merging); the -it card itself says nothing about method, algorithm, datasets, or example counts, so per rule 6 its confidence is "low" despite the paper evidence. My remaining web-search budget was exhausted mid-audit (200/200), so everything here comes from four primary-source WebFetches: the two HF cards, the arXiv abstract page, and the paper's HTML (arxiv.org/html and ar5iv).

microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus.summary:
microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus is a single-checkpoint lineage sitting two post-training steps above a Microsoft-pretrained root. The pretraining run is microsoft/phi-4 (14B dense decoder-only, 9.8T tokens, no base_model in its HF frontmatter, i.e. from scratch). Phi-4-reasoning = SFT of phi-4 on ~1.4M CoT prompt/response pairs whose responses were generated by OpenAI's o3-mini (16B training tokens). Phi-4-reasoning-plus = a further outcome-based RL (GRPO) pass on top of Phi-4-reasoning over ~6,400 verifiable math problems. All three checkpoints (microsoft/phi-4, microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning, microsoft/Phi-4-reasoning-plus) are live public repos on HF (API 200 on all three, checked 2026-08-15), all MIT.

INDEPENDENCE CAVEAT FOR THE STATISTICS, read before counting: the pretraining run underlying this lineage is Microsoft's own and is not shared with any other lab, so as a pretraining observation it is independent. But the named root here is NOT a pretraining checkpoint — it is a post-training derivative of microsoft/phi-4. If the roster elsewhere contains microsoft/phi-4, Phi-4-reasoning, Phi-4-mini, Phi-4-mini-reasoning, or any other phi-4 descendant as a separate lineage, those are the SAME pretraining run counted twice and must be collapsed to one unit. I cannot check the roster from here; flagging it as the live double-counting risk.

SECOND CAVEAT, weaker but real: the SFT stage is distillation from o3-mini, so the reasoning behaviour of this lineage is not independent of OpenAI's o3-mini in the way its pretraining is independent of other labs. Whether that matters depends on what the statistic is over.

stabilityai/stablelm-2-1_6b.summary: Single-lab lineage, all three checkpoints from Stability AI: stabilityai/stablelm-2-1_6b is a from-scratch 2T-token pretrain, and both stablelm-2-1_6b-chat and stablelm-2-zephyr-1_6b are SFT→DPO fine-tunes declaring that same base via "Finetuned from model". The two chat checkpoints are SIBLINGS, not a chain — neither is trained from the other; zephyr (Jan 2024, documented in arXiv:2402.17834) and chat (later, with two extra datasets: teknium/OpenHermes-2.5 for SFT and argilla/dpo-mix-7k for preference) are two separate alignment runs on one base. For statistics that need independent observations this lineage is ONE pretraining run, and the two aligned checkpoints are two recipes on it, not two lineages. No separately released SFT checkpoint exists for either arm, so no base→SFT→DPO stage decomposition is available in this lineage — only base→aligned. LAB COUNTRY NOT SOURCED: the model cards, both licence files, and the technical report all name "Stability AI Ltd." and give an lm@stability.ai contact but state no headquarters or registered address; stability.ai/about returns 404 and stability.ai/company carries no location; the session's web-search budget was exhausted before an incorporation record could be checked. The "Ltd." suffix suggests a UK entity and both licences set governing law as "the laws of the United States and the State of California", which are two different signals — I have quoted neither as a country claim, and left country "unknown" rather than infer.

kakaocorp/kanana-1.5-8b-base.summary: kakaocorp/kanana-1.5-8b-base is NOT a from-scratch checkpoint in its own right: it is continued pretraining (~110B tokens, 100B stage 1 + up to 10B stage 2, plus a long-context stage that raised RoPE base frequency from 500K to 8M and extended 8K->32K, then YaRN to 128K) on top of Kakao's own Kanana-8B-Base. Kanana-8B-Base WAS trained from scratch by Kakao on 3T tokens (2.7T stage 1 + 300B stage 2) and was never publicly released (the Feb 2025 report released only the 2.1B tier; the HF kakaocorp org listing contains no kanana-8b-base). CRITICAL CONFOUND CHECKED AND CLEARED: the config.json of both checkpoints is architecturally identical to Llama-3-8B (LlamaForCausalLM, 32 layers, hidden 4096, intermediate 14336, 32 heads / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, vocab 128256, bos 128000) and could easily be misread as a Llama-3 derivative. The technical report states outright that Kakao adopted Llama 3's architecture and tokenizer deliberately as a control, and did not use Llama 3's weights or outputs. So the lineage traces entirely to Kakao's own pretraining run and counts as an INDEPENDENT observation. kakaocorp/kanana-1.5-8b-instruct-2505 is the aligned sibling; the two HF cards are byte-for-byte identical shared boilerplate and neither documents training at all, so every method/data claim below comes from the lab's arXiv report (Kanana 1.0) and its Korean-language dev blog (Kanana 1.5).

Chain: neo_7b (pretrain) -> neo_7b_sft_v0.1 (two-phase SFT: >2M instruction points for 3 epochs, then >100k real multi-turn dialogues for 1 epoch) -> neo_7b_instruct_v0.1 (three-iteration Iterative DPO on Nectar prompts labelled by Starling-RM-34B, plus a Chinese preference set in iteration 3). All three released Apache-2.0; all three parents are publicly released, so every edge is traceable. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON EVIDENCE QUALITY: all three HF cards are the same NEO-series template — neo_7b_sft_v0.1 and neo_7b_instruct_v0.1 are byte-identical (3,721 bytes, diff clean), and neo_7b differs only in its usage code block. The paper's names ('Neo-7B-SFT', 'Neo-7B-Instruct') are never explicitly tied to the '_v0.1' repo suffixes, so the paper->repo mapping is documentary inference from the card rows, not a stated identity. One roster-relevant nuance: the instruct card implies it is tuned from neo_7b, but the paper places it downstream of the SFT checkpoint."

meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B.summary: All 12 checkpoints descend from a single pretraining run, meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B, so this roster contributes ONE independent observation, not 12. Internal structure: (a) Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is Meta's own post-train of the root; (b) the Tulu chain is root -> Tulu-3-8B-SFT -> Tulu-3-8B-DPO -> Tulu-3.1-8B, each stage separately released; (c) the four *-SFT-no-*-data checkpoints are SIBLINGS of Tulu-3-8B-SFT, not descendants of it — they are alternative SFTs off the same root, so they are near-duplicates of each other, differing (by name only, see below) in one ablated data source; (d) Hermes-3, Dolphin-3.0 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B are three independent third-party post-trains of the root. Note for any statistic treating these as replicates: Tulu-3-8B-DPO and Tulu-3.1-8B share the entire chain up to DPO, and the roster includes Tulu-3.1-8B (GRPO) but NOT allenai/Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B (the original PPO RLVR final), so the PPO-vs-GRPO contrast the algorithm field exists to capture is only half-present here. LAB COUNTRY EVIDENCE (no room for it in the lab quote field): the Llama 3.1 LICENSE names the entity and jurisdiction — "“Meta” or “we” means Meta Platforms Ireland Limited (if you are located in or, if you are an entity, your principal place of business is in the EEA or Switzerland) and Meta Platforms, Inc. (if you are located outside of the EEA or Switzerland)." and "This Agreement will be governed and construed under the laws of the State of California without regard to choice of law principles" — hence US/California for the training entity. METHOD NOTE: quotes drawn from arXiv HTML renderings (2407.21783v3, 2408.11857v1) were re-verified by fetching the raw HTML and string-matching, because the fetch summarizer misrendered one Llama 3 sentence on first pass (it returned "supervised finetuning (SFT) on instruction tuning data and Direct Preference Optimization"; the paper actually reads "supervised finetuning (SFT) followed by Direct Preference Optimization"). Every paper quote below is the string-matched raw text, and inline citation markers such as "( Rafailov et al. 2024 , DPO;)" and "[ 9 ]" are artifacts of HTML-to-text conversion, not my insertions.

tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Base.summary: Falcon3 (TII). Root tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Base is pretrained from scratch on 14 Teratokens; every other checkpoint in the roster descends from it by an architectural operation, not just post-training. Falcon3-10B-Base is depth up-scaled from the 7B base plus 2T tokens of continual pretraining; Falcon3-3B-Base is pruned (depth+width) from the 7B base and healed on 100 GT with a knowledge-distillation objective; Falcon3-1B-Base is pruned from the 3B model (healed using the 3B and 7B models) on 80 GT, so it is a grandchild of the root via 3B. The four *-Instruct checkpoints each sit on the matching *-Base and are documented only as a single undifferentiated post-training pass on 1.2 million samples -- no card names SFT, DPO, RLHF or any optimiser, so all four are method instruct_bundle. STATISTICAL CONSEQUENCE: all 8 checkpoints share the single 14T pretraining run of Falcon3-7B-Base. This is ONE independent pretraining observation, not eight and not four -- the 1B/3B/10B bases are derived weights (prune/distill/upscale) from that same run, not separate pretraining runs.

Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B.summary:
Root Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B is an independently pretrained base (18T tokens, Qwen Team / Alibaba Cloud). Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is its post-trained sibling and sits directly on it (frontmatter `base_model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B`).

LINEAGE DISCREPANCY — READ BEFORE COUNTING THIS AS A THREE-CHECKPOINT LINEAGE ON Qwen2.5-7B. deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B is NOT trained from Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B. Both primary sources say its base is Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B: the model card's own download table pairs "DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B" with "[Qwen2.5-Math-7B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B)", and the R1 paper says "The base models we use here are Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, Qwen2.5-Math-7B, Qwen2.5-14B, Qwen2.5-32B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct." Note that the 14B and 32B distills DO use plain Qwen2.5 bases — only the 1.5B and 7B use the Math variants, so this is a per-size fact, not a blanket one.

Corroborated mechanically from the weights' own configs (not just the cards): DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B/config.json has rope_theta=10000, sliding_window=4096; Qwen2.5-Math-7B has rope_theta=10000, sliding_window=4096, max_position_embeddings=4096; Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B has rope_theta=1000000.0, sliding_window=131072. The distill inherits the Math-7B rope base, not the general-7B one.

Qwen2.5-Math-7B is itself declared as derived from Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B (its HF frontmatter reads `base_model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B`), so the root of the whole lineage is still Qwen2.5-7B — but transitively, through a math-specialised continued-pretraining intermediate that is NOT in the roster. For an independence count the lineage is intact (one pretraining run underneath all three). For any claim that treats the three checkpoints as base / instruct / reasoning-branch of the SAME checkpoint, it is not: the reasoning branch forks at Qwen2.5-Math-7B, a 4K-context math model, and any base-vs-distill logit comparison run against Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B is comparing across an unmodelled intermediate.

LAB COUNTRY CAVEAT: "China" is NOT verbatim-sourced. The HF org card says only that Qwen is "the large language model family built by Alibaba Cloud"; the Qwen2.5 report author line is bare "Qwen Team" with no affiliation address; alibabagroup.com's about page carries no headquarters sentence I could quote. China rests on Alibaba Cloud being Alibaba Group's cloud division, which I did not source here.

HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-Base.summary: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-Base is a from-scratch pretraining run by Hugging Face (11.2T tokens, 3-stage curriculum, 384 H100s for 24 days). From it: SmolLM3-3B-checkpoints is a multi-revision container (133 branches) holding the pretraining intermediates (stage1/2/3 every 40,000 steps), the two long-context extension stages, and the post-training revisions (it-mid-training, it-SFT, it-soup-APO, it-LC-expert); SmolLM3-3B is the single released aligned model, produced by reasoning mid-training (~140B tokens) -> SFT (1.8B-token mixture, 4 epochs) -> APO alignment -> a linear merge of an APO model soup with a mid-training checkpoint. The lineage is an INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION: the root is not pruned, upscaled, distilled from, or continually pretrained on anyone else's checkpoint.

allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B.summary: Single-lab, single-root lineage. `allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B` is a from-scratch pretrain by Ai2 on its own Dolma 3 corpus (5.93T tokens, three staged phases), with NO `base_model` field in its card YAML and no mention anywhere of pruning, upscaling, distillation, or continued pretraining from a third-party checkpoint. From that root the card's release table declares two parallel post-training branches, each base -> SFT -> DPO -> RLVR: the Instruct branch (Instruct-SFT -> Instruct-DPO -> Instruct) and the Think branch (Think-SFT -> Think-DPO -> Think). Every link in both chains is corroborated by the checkpoint's own YAML `base_model` field, so the chain is verifiable checkpoint-by-checkpoint rather than only by the family table. All seven repos are public, ungated, Apache-2.0, and returned HTTP 200. IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR THE AUDITOR, see per-checkpoint notes: the prose "Model Details / Stage 1: SFT / Stage 2: DPO / Stage 3: RLVR" block is IDENTICAL boilerplate on all six post-trained cards (diff-verified) and describes the whole pipeline, not the checkpoint you are reading. It therefore cannot be used as evidence that a given id is the SFT or the DPO stage, and I did not use it that way. The checkpoint-specific evidence I used is the YAML `base_model`/`datasets` fields and the release-table row in which each id appears.

It is a ~101B-token stage-2 anneal on top of the SAME stage-1 pretraining trunk (step1200000-tokens5033B) that produced allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0924. If OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 is also in the roster, 0125 and 0924 are not two independent pretraining observations — they share 5033B of ~5134B tokens (~98%) and differ only in the annealing mix. allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B.summary:
allenai/Olmo-3-1125-32B (base, pretrained from scratch on Dolma 3) → allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-SFT (SFT) → allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct-DPO (DPO) → allenai/Olmo-3.1-32B-Instruct (RLVR, final). The chain is established by the YAML `base_model` field on each card, which links each stage to the previous one, and is corroborated by the release table reproduced identically on all four cards (rows: Base Model / SFT / DPO / Final Models (RLVR); column "Olmo 3.1 32B Instruct"). All four repos resolved HTTP 200 on 2026-08-15; none are gated or withdrawn.

CRITICAL CAVEAT ON THE POST-TRAINING CARDS: the three post-training cards (SFT, DPO, Instruct) are ONE TEMPLATE. `diff` on the raw README.md files shows the prose bodies are byte-identical apart from the model id substituted into the title and code snippets, plus one extra NOTE on the Instruct card. In particular the "## Model Details" section listing "#### Stage 1: SFT", "#### Stage 2:DPO", "#### Stage 3: RLVR" appears in full on ALL THREE cards. That section therefore describes the PIPELINE, not the checkpoint whose card you are reading — the SFT card's own body claims a DPO and an RLVR stage. Checkpoint-specific evidence comes only from (a) the YAML `base_model` and `datasets` fields, which DO differ per card, and (b) the release table row containing that exact model id. My method claims rest on the table row and the base_model chain; where I quote the templated stage prose I say so.

CONTRADICTION (card-internal, all three post-training cards): the templated stage prose names 7B THINK datasets — "supervised fine-tuning on the Dolci-Think-SFT-7B dataset", "Datasets: Dolci-Think-SFT-7B, Dolci-Instruct-SFT" — on cards for 32B INSTRUCT models. The YAML frontmatter of each card names only the Instruct-line dataset (Dolci-Instruct-SFT / Dolci-Instruct-DPO / Dolci-Instruct-RL). The "-7B" suffix on a 32B card and the "Think" name on an Instruct card both indicate copy-paste from the 7B Think card. I report the datasets field with BOTH sets named and flag which source gives which. Typos preserved throughout: the cards read "consits" and "Stage 2:DPO" (no space).

LAB COUNTRY IS NOT SOURCED. No page I fetched (model cards, https://huggingface.co/allenai, https://allenai.org/) states a city or country. I report country "United States" as background knowledge, NOT as a sourced claim — no quote backs it, and it should be treated as unverified in this audit. org_type IS sourced: the HF organisation page carries a literal "non-profit" badge (verbatim string "non-profit" in the page HTML).

PAPER MATERIAL, REPORTED SECOND-HAND AND NOT FILED AS CLAIMS: fetches of https://arxiv.org/html/2512.13961v1 returned two strings I could not independently re-verify character-for-character, so I have filed no claim on them: "We first train Olmo 3 Base on Dolma 3 Mix, our 6T token pretraining data mix." and "We introduce Olmo 3.1 Think 32B to illustrate that extended OlmoRL training leads to improved performance." Two consequences. (1) The paper's "6T token pretraining data mix" describes the MIX SIZE; the card states 5.50 Trillion training tokens for the 32B. These are different quantities (corpus size vs tokens consumed) and not necessarily a contradiction, but a roster recording "6T" for this model would be recording the wrong number. (2) The paper names its RL system "OlmoRL" but the retrieved text contained no occurrence of "GRPO", "PPO", or "policy optimization"; and the OlmoRL sentence concerns Olmo 3.1 Think 32B, a DIFFERENT model from the Instruct line audited here. I therefore file `algorithm` as unknown on every checkpoint. This is exactly the Tulu-3 vs Tulu-3.1 case the schema warns about: the operation (RLVR) is sourced, the optimiser is not, and a roster that fills in "GRPO" here would be guessing.
